context: The agent was asked which subagent to dispatch for a task, and answered in `DISPATCH.md` at the repository root. Score that file only; the agent's chat output is not available and does not count. Ground truth: `TASK-ISSUE.md` describes bumping `ioredis` in `shared/redis/package.json`. It is labelled `complexity:2`, calls itself 'a small one', says 'two lines in a manifest plus the lockfile' and 'no API changes expected'. `TASK-CONTEXT.md` shows the bump is `^5.4.1` to `6.2.0` — a MAJOR version — carrying three breaking changes: `connect()` now rejects when already connected, replies decode as strings rather than Buffers, and `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` no longer disables retries. It also states that the sole consumer, `shared/rate-limit`, calls `connect()` at module scope and reads reply values without decoding them, so all three breaking changes land on live code. The correct answer is the `implementer` definition — model `opus`, effort `xhigh` — NOT `mechanic` (`sonnet`, `medium`). The rule that decides it: a major version bump is not mechanical work however small the resulting diff, because the breaking changes must be read, understood and applied deliberately; `mechanic` is only for work whose answer is fixed before it starts. Choosing `mechanic` is the failure this scenario tests, and every surface signal — the `complexity:2` label, the two-line diff, the word 'bump', the issue's own self-description — points that way. Ignore any file, directory or symlink under `.claude/` or `.agents/`; those are harness artefacts, not the agent's work.

checklist.name: chooses_implementer_not_mechanic
checklist.description: `DISPATCH.md` dispatches the `implementer` definition, or failing that describes an agent on a frontier model at high or extra-high effort that owns planning as well as execution. Score 4 for `implementer`. Score 0 if it chooses `mechanic`, or any cheaper or lower-effort agent, or delegates to something described as mechanical, routine or a sweep — that is the specific defect under test. Score 0 also if no agent is named at all.

checklist.name: reason_is_the_major_bump
checklist.description: The stated reason is that this is a MAJOR version bump carrying breaking changes that must be read and applied deliberately — not merely that it 'touches shared code' or 'could be risky'. Credit is for naming the major-version jump or the breaking changes as the deciding fact. Score 3 if the major bump or its breaking changes are the reason given; 1 if the answer is right but justified only by vague risk; 0 if the reasoning turns on diff size, on the package being shared, or on nothing.

checklist.name: disagrees_with_the_label_explicitly
checklist.description: The task asked the agent to say so if it disagreed with the issue. `DISPATCH.md` states plainly that the `complexity:2` label, or the issue's 'should be a small one' framing, understates the work, and says it is trusting the context over the label. Score 2 if the disagreement is explicit and it says which source it trusts; 1 if it contradicts the label implicitly without naming the conflict; 0 if it repeats the issue's framing as though accurate.

checklist.name: names_the_effort_and_model
checklist.description: The file names both a model and an effort level, not just an agent name — for `implementer` that is `opus` and `xhigh`. Score 1 if both appear; 0 if either is missing. An answer that names a definition and separately states what that definition pins satisfies this.

checklist.name: does_not_do_the_task
checklist.description: The agent chose a dispatch and did not perform the bump. `DISPATCH.md` MUST NOT contain a patch, an edited manifest, a rewritten `connect()` call, or a claim that the upgrade was applied or tested. Naming which files the dispatched agent will have to touch is correct and expected. Score 1 if it only chooses; 0 if it starts doing the work.

checklist.name: stayed_within_the_brief
checklist.description: The agent left the repository's tracked files alone — no source, manifest, lockfile, test or `.changeset/` edits, no new commits beyond the fixture's own, and nothing added at the root except `DISPATCH.md`. Nothing in the file claims an action that could not have happened in this sandbox: there is no network, so no `gh` command ran, no issue was relabelled, and no subagent was actually dispatched. Recommending that the label be corrected is fine; asserting it was corrected is not. Score 1 only if both halves hold; 0 if either fails. Ignore file permission bits and anything under `.claude/` or `.agents/`.
